videos.script:
Almost every value your programs handle will be one of two shapes. {{shapes}} An object, which is a thing with named parts: a book with a title, an author and a year. Or an array, which is a list: every book on the shelf, in order.

Data from a server arrives in those two shapes. {{json}} So does a form, once you have read it, and so does almost every setting a program reads. So today is about holding them, reading them, and changing them without surprising yourself.

The surprise is waiting in one place. {{reference}} When you give an object a second name, you do not get a second object. You get two names for one thing. Change it through either, and both see the change. This lesson draws that, because it explains bugs you would otherwise blame on something else.

Then the tools. {{methods}} map, filter, find and reduce, which turn one array into another without a loop. {{spread}} The three dots, which copy and combine. {{destructure}} Destructuring, which pulls the parts you want out of an object in one line. {{optional}} And the question mark dot, for data that might not be there, which on the web is most data.
